title: Borel pairs and actual rho section modules
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Semisimple means smooth, affine, connected and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, where solvable means that the successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and central means commuting with every element after every scalar extension. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\ge0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$; a maximal torus is one not contained in a larger torus. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. There exist a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$. For every such pair, let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots given by the nonzero characters of the adjoint action of $T$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, where $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ is the kernel of $B(F[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2))\to B(F)$, with its tangent-space structure. A character is a group-scheme homomorphism $T\to\mathbf G_m$; addition of characters means multiplication of their values. The character lattice $X^*(T)$ contains $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$. It has an extension $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$; this radical is its largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, with unipotent meaning that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. For every integer $m\ge1$, define the actual subspace of the coordinate algebra
$$W_m=\{f\in F[S]: f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m f(g)\text{ for every }F\text{-algebra }A,\ g\in S(A),\ b\in B(A)\}.$$
With the left-translation action $(s f)(g)=f(s^{-1}g)$, $W_m$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional rational $S$-module. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with a coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$ satisfying the coassociativity and counit identities; $V^S=\{v:\rho_V(v)=v\otimes1\}$. Tensor products have diagonal coaction. All equivariance and invariance below mean identities of coactions, equivalently identities after every commutative $F$-algebra extension.

source.place: Definition 17.6 and Theorems 17.9--17.10 (pp.353--355); Definition 19.22 and following paragraph (p.402); 22.11 (p.465), Definition 22.21 and Proposition 22.27 (pp.468--470), 22.48--22.49 (pp.479--480). The function convention is Alper, §9.7 immediately preceding Lemma 9.7.2 (right semi-invariance with positive exponent), opposite to Milne E(lambda).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], a semisimple group is reductive. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] to obtain $T\subseteq B\subseteq S$. Fix any such pair. The same node gives the root datum, its positive system in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, $B=U\rtimes T$ with projection $p$, and the proper finite-type flag quotient $Q=S/B$. These assertions require neither characteristic zero nor nontrivial rank.

proof.text: Work in $X\otimes\mathbf Q$, not in the field $F$, so division by $2$ here also makes sense in characteristic $2$. For a simple root $\alpha_i$, the reflection $s_i$ permutes $\Phi^+\setminus\{\alpha_i\}$: the coefficients of every other simple root are unchanged by $s_i(\beta)=\beta-\langle\beta,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\alpha_i$; a positive root $\beta\ne\alpha_i$ has a positive coefficient at another simple root, since the root system is reduced, and thus its image cannot be negative. Consequently $s_i(\rho)=\rho-\alpha_i$, whence $\langle\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=1$. By [lem-sfb-simply-connected-character-lattice], $\rho=\sum_i\omega_i\in X$. Define $\widetilde\rho=\rho\circ p$; this is a character extending $\rho$ and trivial on $U$. For every $m\ge1$, $m\rho$ is dominant since all its simple-coroot pairings equal $m$. Empty sums give $\rho=0$ in rank zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dominant-character-highest-line] to $\lambda=m\rho$ to obtain $V$ and $v\ne0$ with $b v=\widetilde\rho(b)^m v$. Choose $\ell\in V^\vee$ with $\ell(v)=1$. The matrix coefficient $f(g)=\ell(gv)$ is a regular function because the representation is rational. For every $F$-algebra $A$, $f(gb)=\ell(g(bv))=\widetilde\rho(b)^m\ell(gv)$, so $f\in W_m$, and $f(1)=1$ proves $W_m\ne0$. This constructs a member of the actual specified subspace of $F[S]$.

proof.text: Set $\chi=-m\widetilde\rho$ in additive character notation, so $\chi(b)^{-1}=\widetilde\rho(b)^m$. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], the actual space $W_m$ identifies with $\Gamma(Q,\mathcal L_\chi)$. Here $Q$ is proper over $F$ and $\mathcal L_\chi$ is coherent. Apply the affine-base finiteness clause of [lem-pc-coherent-hi] in degree zero over the Noetherian ring $F$: $\Gamma(Q,\mathcal L_\chi)$ is a finite $F$-module, hence $W_m$ is finite dimensional.

source.place: Tag 02O6, lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite, with Milne Section 18c and Theorem 22.48 for the section identification.

proof.text: Write $H=F[S]$ and $K=F[B]$. The semi-invariance condition is the kernel of the linear map $D:H\to H\otimes K$, $D(f)=r^*f-f\otimes\widetilde\rho^m$, where $r:S\times B\to S$ is right multiplication. Left translation is the regular coaction $c:H\to H\otimes H$ determined by $c(f)(g,s)=f(s^{-1}g)$. The two group actions commute, since $(s^{-1}g)b=s^{-1}(gb)$, and hence $(D\otimes1)c(f)=0$ for $f\in\ker D$. Tensoring with an $F$-vector space preserves kernels (choose a basis, making tensoring a direct sum), so $c(W_m)\subseteq W_m\otimes H$. Restrict $c$ to obtain the required rational coaction; its coassociativity and counit follow by restriction from the group identities for left translation. The displayed computation also gives $(s f)(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^m(s f)(g)$ over every $F$-algebra. Thus the action is on the specified finite-dimensional nonzero subspace, with all identities scheme-theoretic.
